lead: At the northern end of Sant Andreu, next to the Meridiana, named after a chapel from 1413.
text: Before it was a neighbourhood it was the Coll de Finestrelles, the edge of the old municipality of Sant Andreu de Palomar, and its name comes from the chapel of la Trinitat, built in 1413. It was an almost deserted area, with few farmhouses (masies), the best known being Can Cagamantes, and vineyards on the higher ground that lasted until the 1950s. In 1992 the Nus de la Trinitat interchange was built, and the Pla de Barris 2025-2028 allocates 14.5 million euros to Trinitat Vella, Bon Pastor and Baró de Viver together.

Between 1952 and 1954 its appearance changed, with blocks of flats built over the vineyards, and in 1961 the extension of Avinguda Meridiana opened: with the new roads, La Trinitat ended up split into two neighbourhoods, La Trinitat Nova and La Trinitat Vella, which are sometimes confused. With 11,307 inhabitants in 0.81 km², its community life revolves around sports clubs with decades of history, such as CD Trinidad, founded in 1928, and CD Cerro, founded in 1960 and Catalan champion in the 1971-72 season. At 2,206 €/m² and 682 €/month, it has the second-lowest sale price in Sant Andreu, behind only Baró de Viver. If you are selling, the average sale price is 36% below the Sant Andreu average. Within the neighbourhood, the price of each flat depends on its condition, its floor and its building, so it is best to compare it with nearby sales rather than with the district average. If you are buying, an 80 m² flat costs about 176,000 € on average, and this neighbourhood sits in the middle band of Sant Andreu (6th of 7 by price). If you are investing, the average rent is 25% below the district; before deciding, it is worth studying each deal with real figures for purchase, renovation and rental income.
housing: Blocks of flats from the 1950s onwards, in a compact neighbourhood next to the Meridiana.
